_why: Mystery Player answers must be people known FIRST as footballers. Alex, 2026-08-14: 'some players go into management yes, but it is a bit misleading if some players had a way bigger career as a manager than as a player. Xavi, Xabi Alonso are good mystery players — they are managers nowadays but known as great footballers. Alex Ferguson also played at a high level but everyone knows him as a manager, so he would not fit.' The pool carries no occupation field and FAME CANNOT SEPARATE THESE — Ferguson scores 113, higher than Platini — so this list is curated by hand and is the only reliable filter.
_kept_deliberately: Deschamps, Simeone, Mancini and Conte are NOT excluded. All four had genuinely elite playing careers (a World Cup-winning captain, an Argentina mainstay, a Sampdoria great, a five-time Serie A winner) and are known as players as well as managers — the Xavi/Xabi Alonso category. Move any of them into `managers` below if you disagree; that is the only edit needed.
_how_to_extend: Add the exact `name` string from mysteryPool.json. gen-mystery-schedule.mjs refuses to schedule anything listed here, and scripts/verify-mystery-answers.mjs fails the build if one slips into the schedule.
_guardiola_note: Guardiola is a genuinely hard call and sits in `managers` as the cautious default. He was a real Barcelona and Spain midfielder, but his managerial fame now dwarfs it by any measure — which is exactly the test. Move him to `_kept_deliberately` if you'd rather have him.
_notFootballers_note: O. J. Simpson was in the CURATED ANSWER SET at fame 61 with club 'Buffalo Bills'. American football. He would have been served as a daily football puzzle. Not an editorial judgement — a data error, and the reason this file also carries a hard sport check. Julio Iglesias was caught the same way, during the manager sweep: a Real Madrid youth goalkeeper before a car crash ended it, in the answer set at fame level with club 'Real Madrid Club de Fútbol'. Famous-for-something-else is its own failure mode, separate from managers, and neither fame nor club can detect it.
